function: Learns the beamfocusing phase matrix (per-element phase shifts) of a programmable metasurface so power focuses on a near-field desired focal point without CSI (pp. 4-5).
system: Programmable-metasurface radiating aperture (ELPM), 60x60=3600 elements (100 subarrays of 6x6), 3/4-bit phase shifters, lambda/2 spacing; receive antenna at focal point; 28 GHz (pp. 3, 10, 12).
method: TD3 deep RL agent per subarray; transfer learning via policy propagation (circular-correlation teacher choice), quasi-liquid-layer fine-tuning, and policy blending; CSI-free, reward from measured power (pp. 5-10).
data_channel: Custom simulated multipath room channel, 4x4x3 m, as in [23], reflection coefficient 0.1, path-loss exponent 2.7; agent trains online on simulated power feedback, no dataset (pp. 10, 12).
test_conditions: Same simulated room, default DFP (1,1.5,1.4) m; 3/4-bit phase shifters; blending tested on random new DFPs 1-2 m away with 10 or 50 stored policies (pp. 10, 13).
baselines: Learned: DRL (TD3) without transfer as in [23] (No-TL); ablations PP-HighECC without QLL and PP-LowECC. Non-learned: exact-CSI in-phase focusing target (p. 12).
metrics: Normalized power density at the focal point, beamfocusing radius (BFR), and training iterations to convergence (speed-up factor) (pp. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 10: "considered a multipath channel model in a 4 × 4 × 3 m3 room". Not met: the channel is a custom multipath simulator defined by eq. (1) on p. 3 (path-loss exponent, reflection coefficients); no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 3: "Instead of training a new policy from scratch" ... "previously trained policies learned for different DFP locations"; p. 13: "for a new DFP, the policy blending scheme is run by selecting K-blending component policies", reaching convergence "which is 8.3 times faster than the No-TL scenario".
q3_support: p. 12: "DRL with no TL as in [23] denoted by No-TL" (earlier DRL of the same authors); p. 13: "the focused power density at the DFP is enhanced by about 20%" (performance metric); p. 12: "normalized target power density, which is computed by using the exact CSI of all array elements" and "the power has reached 98% of the target value" (non-learned reference).
q4_support: p. 12: "at only 25 k iterations"; p. 13: "which is 8.3 times faster than the No-TL scenario". Not met: only training iterations to convergence are given; no FLOPs, parameter count, runtime or complexity order; p. 2: "significantly reduces the complexity" is qualitative.
q5_support: p. 10: "considered a multipath channel model in a 4 × 4 × 3 m3 room". Not met: the channel is simulated; no code or data link or DOI, no public channel dataset and no measured data appear anywhere in the 15 pages.
notes: Area 3: the learned DRL policy sets the phase-shift (beamfocusing) matrix of a programmable metasurface aperture to focus power at a near-field point (pp. 4-5). ris=1 because the aperture is an extremely large-scale programmable metasurface (ELPM) with learned per-element phases; the paper describes it as a radiating phased-array aperture (p. 3), never calls it a RIS and does not describe a reflecting link, so the reviewer may set ris=0 if only reflecting surfaces count. q2: transfer to a new focal point after policy blending, not retraining from scratch (pp. 3, 13). q3 needs confirmation: the learned baseline is the earlier DRL of the same authors [23] (No-TL, p. 12), which is also the proposed method without its transfer modules, and the non-learned comparison is the exact-CSI in-phase target, an upper bound rather than a competing blind scheme (p. 12). q4: only training-iteration counts are reported, which the reviewer may judge as training effort rather than computational cost. The 28 GHz frequency and the room, reflection and path-loss values come from Table I on p. 12, read from the page image because the table is not in the extracted text.
